records.text:
#Add This One Ingredient to Beet Juice and Double the Blood Flow Effect

Are you drinking beet juice for better circulation but still experiencing cold hands, numb feet, or aching legs? After 65, changes in the body's nitric oxide production system may affect how well your blood vessels function. In this video, Dr. Cale Smith explains why adding L-citrulline to beet juice may support circulation through two different nitric oxide pathways.

Discover how beet juice provides dietary nitrates that help the body produce nitric oxide, encouraging blood vessels to relax and supporting blood flow. You'll also learn about the endothelial pathway, the eNOS enzyme, and how age-related changes in arginase activity can affect the availability of L-arginine needed for nitric oxide production.

The featured ingredient is L-citrulline — an amino acid your kidneys convert into L-arginine. The video explains why this process may help bypass some of the metabolic barriers associated with aging and how L-citrulline and beet juice may complement each other to support vascular function.

You'll also explore clinical research involving older adults, including findings on femoral blood flow, vascular conductance, arterial flexibility, and exercise performance. Plus, learn the practical morning routine discussed in the video, including beetroot juice, L-citrulline powder, fresh lemon juice, timing, and the potential role of quercetin-rich foods such as red onion.

If you're over 60 and interested in healthy circulation, nitric oxide production, vascular health, and cardiovascular aging, this video breaks down the science behind this combination and what the research actually shows.

💬 Join the conversation: Have you heard of L-citrulline before? Tell me your age, whether you've tried beet juice, and what you hope to improve. Share your thoughts in the comments!

Subscribe to Dr. Cale Smith for more research-focused videos about preventive health, healthy aging, circulation, and cardiovascular wellness.

📚 Research Sources:

1. Le Roux-Mallouf et al. — Nitrate + Citrulline in older adults (60–70) — *Aging*, 2019 — aging-us.com/article/101984
2. Gonzales JU et al. — L-Citrulline improves exercise blood flow in older adults — *Experimental Physiology*, 2017 — doi.org/10.1113/EP086587
3. Chen Y et al. — L-Citrulline improves FMD & arterial stiffness in elderly (meta-analysis, 8 RCTs) — *Frontiers in Nutrition*, 2025 — doi.org/10.3389/fnut.2025.1632952
4. Shanely RA et al. — L-Citrulline improves vascular endothelial function — *British Journal of Nutrition*, 2022 — doi.org/10.1017/S0007114521004104
5. Lacchini S et al. — Arginase elevated in aged tissue, competes with eNOS — *Oxidative Medicine & Cellular Longevity*, 2019 — PMC6530149
6. PubMed — Declining nitric oxide bioavailability in cardiovascular aging — *PubMed*, 2025 — PMID: 41953454

Disclaimer: This video is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Beet juice and L-citrulline are not replacements for prescribed medication or medical care. If you have cardiovascular disease, circulation problems, take blood pressure medication, or are considering supplements, consult your healthcare professional before making changes to your routine.

#BeetJuice #LCitrulline #BloodCirculation #HealthyAging #Over60Health #NitricOxide #VascularHealth #seniorhealth
